summary.tpReason: Telemetry shows a coordinated, successful intrusion: the same Russian source IP used successful Okta privilege/MFA tampering and AWS abuse, followed by GCP creation of a named backdoor service account, key issuance, owner-level IAM grants, resource abuse, sensitive-object reads, and logging suppression. These are not benign deployment indicators.
summary.fpReason: No credible benign explanation is supported. All relevant GCP operations succeeded, used attacker-named resources (backdoor-svc-gcp, crypto-miner instances, allow-all-ingress), and were corroborated by matching Okta/AWS activity from the same source IP.
summary.whatHappened: On 2026-08-19, mirage@pkwork.onmicrosoft.com logged into Okta at 16:33 UTC from 198.51.100.42 (Moscow/RU), granted super-admin, created an API token, and altered MFA including enrolling an attacker-controlled TOTP. The account then abused AWS and GCP. In GCP project pocaas-prod-01 from 17:49:10-18:01:05 UTC, it created backdoor-svc-gcp, created key abc123def456, granted it roles/owner, opened allow-all-ingress, created crypto-miner-01/02, read financial-report-2026.xlsx, employee-pii-export.csv, and api-keys-production.json, disabled/deleted logging sinks, and granted itself Token Creator on deploy-pipeline. The backdoor service account created crypto-miner-03 at 17:59:05 UTC.
keyEvidence: GCPAuditLogs: 17:49:10-18:01:05 UTC, 13 successful operations by mirage from caller IP 198.51.100.42; zero failures. Created backdoor-svc-gcp and key abc123def456, then granted roles/owner.
GCPAuditLogs: mirage successfully read sensitive objects financial-report-2026.xlsx, employee-pii-export.csv, and api-keys-production.json at 17:55:15, 17:55:40, and 18:00:50 UTC.
GCPAuditLogs: mirage opened 0.0.0.0/0 all-protocol ingress and created crypto-miner-01/02; backdoor-svc-gcp created crypto-miner-03 at 17:59:05 UTC.
GCPAuditLogs: mirage deleted export-all-logs and disabled the _Default sink at 17:56:55-17:57:35 UTC, evidencing defense evasion.
OktaV2_CL: successful 16:33-16:37 UTC login and privilege/MFA tampering from 198.51.100.42 in Moscow/RU; MFA was enrolled for an attacker-controlled device.

AWSCloudTrail: same IP/account performed CreateUser, CreateAccessKey, AdministratorAccess attachment, unrestricted ingress, five GPU instances, sensitive S3 reads, and StopLogging from 16:49:17-17:05:25 UTC.
researchDone: Reviewed GCPAuditLogs for the alert window and surrounding period, including request/response, authorization, caller IP, resource, and status; all mirage GCP operations succeeded.
Searched GCP after 18:01:05 UTC through 00:00 UTC for mirage, backdoor-svc-gcp, and key abc123def456; found no additional matching activity beyond the final IAM grant.
Reviewed OktaV2_CL for mirage from 15:30-17:00 UTC; found successful session, super-admin grant, API token creation, and MFA tampering from RU.
Reviewed AWSCloudTrail from 16:40-17:10 UTC; found successful persistence, data access, compute abuse, unrestricted ingress, and StopLogging from the same IP.
Checked GCP activity for failures and external corroboration; eve.hacker@external-domain.com had two denied operations, while mirage had 13 successes.
Checked sign_in_adelete_CL for mirage in the alert window; no matching records were present, so this source does not corroborate or refute the cloud activity.
